Hi Brian,

The RRO Installer currently does not log any info about the install, so we have no good way of knowing what might be the problem here.

One thing you could do, if you are willing to investigate the problem further from your end, would be to install the Windows application 'Process Monitor'.  Process Monitor will report detailed problems on Windows applications and you can configure it to create a output log file. If you can do that and email us the resulting log file, we can take a closer look at the problem.

Here is more information on how to use Process Monitor:
http://www.winhelponline.com/blog/process-monitor-track-events-generate-log-file/

If you can do this and monitor the RRO Windows installer executable, that might help us track down the problem.

Stephen Weller
Revolution R Open Technical Support

messages.subject_clean: Error installing MKL Math Libraries after installing RRO 3.2.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ronald,

This is a known problem with the MKL Installer on Windows when installing as a user who does not have administrative rights.
The MKL Installer needs administrative rights to successfully install on Windows systems.

Unfortunately, their is currently no way around this. You will need to have someone with admin rights install the software for you on your system.

Stephen Weller
Revolution R Open Technical Support

messages.body_plain:
According to Intel, they have options for forcing computations onto the Phis. They also claim that the MKL will send calcs to the Phis, automatically, when the MKL decided the calc is large enough. I guess it tries to determine what is "best" for your system.

Have you tried exceedingly large matrix calcs? I've been working on large matrices say 100,000x100,000 and raising them to large powers, like 10,000. (I had to reinstall everything on my Phi workstation after I did my benchmarking. If I turned the Phis off 'Automatic_Offload = 0', RRO used 1% of my processor, or less.) When I get it up an running again, I will look at how large you need to go to get the Phis to do their thing.

Another option is to use the AMD ACML. From what I have read, it has an automatic offload option onto GPUs and possibly the Phis. It uses OpenCl to do this. I purchased a couple powerful and cheap AMD GPUs. I'm taking a class this fall in C++ with the hopes it will make me a better programmer when it comes to compiling the ACML.

Have you read about the newer generation of Phis? The Knights Landing version can actually replace the main processor on your board. They also have huge amounts of DDR4 ECC Ram. One item I saw had 384GB of Ram.

messages.subject_clean: [RRO] install RRO on fedora 22 - dependency issue
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

RRO is an enhanced distribution of R; therefore you do not need to install both RRO and R separately.  As a prerequisite to DeployR <http://deployr.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/admin/install/#depend>, you can install either RRO or R.  However, please note that Fedora is not a supported platform at this time for either RRO or DeployR. For a list of supported platforms for RRO, see here <https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/download/>.

— Josée

Josée Martens
Revolution Analytics, a Microsoft company

messages.subject: RRO and Intel MKL
messages.subject_clean: RRO and Intel MKL
messages.body_plain:
I have been using R and Intel MKL for a while. Now I am surprised by
two things when it comes to install RRO and MKL.

- as RRO is open source licensed, why use Intel MKL, proprietary paid
licenced, to provide Blas ? Why not use open openblas[1] instead?
- your documentation refers to install RRO then install MKL. Why not
install Blas library first, then build RRO with "./configure
--with-blas=" as mentioned in intel article[2] ?

Thank you for hints.

[1]http://www.openblas.net/
[2]https://software.intel.com/en-us/articles/build-r-301-with-intel-c-compiler-and-intel-mkl-on-linux

--

messages.body_plain:
I have installed RRO 3.2.1 in an Ubuntu machine in which there was an CRAN R version and RStudio.
I see that /usr/bin/R now points to the RRO (/usr/bin/R --> /usr//lib64/RRO-3.2.1/R-3.2.1/lib/R/bin/R ) and the starting message in Rstudio informs that it is using the RRO version with MKL.

However, when I try to plot something as simple as

plot(1:10)

I get this error

Error in RStudioGD() :
 Shadow graphics device error: r error 4 (R code execution error)
In addition: Warning message:
In grDevices:::png("/tmp/RtmpR8RPl1/452e73a80ef34f46977c4cc704c4b35d.png",  :
unable to open connection to X11 display ''

I have installed additional Ubuntu packages like the following ones with no results (of course, I restarted Rstudio after any instalation)
sudo apt-get install libx11-dev libxt-dev libpango1.0-dev r-cran-cairodevice

I am using a machine without display, but I did this previously on other similar machine without any problem.
In some forum I read that perhaps I have to compile RRO from sources with flags for not using xlib.
Do you have any information about this?

Best regards,

-Mariano

messages.subject: Re: RRO and Intel MKL
messages.subject_clean: RRO and Intel MKL
messages.body_plain:
Hi Arnaud,

We use the MKL because in our research it provides the best performance on a wide range of platforms. We're pleased that we're able to partner with Intel to offer it to all RRO users free of charge, as an optional add-on to Revolution R Open.

You're welcome to build RRO (or R) from source using the BLAS library of your choice. Our build instructions at https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO/blob/master/README.md are a good starting point. The R Core Group also provide some useful tips for building R with other BLAS libraries at:
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-admin.html#BLAS

Hope this helps,
# David Smith
